text:
Connor Dewar is a fourth-line forward on a Pittsburgh team that is losing a lot and, by most reports, getting ready to sell. He plays about 13 minutes a night, hits, blocks shots, and has five points in 24 games.

The last ten games have been empty: no points, where we'd expect about three at his ice time, and his line has been on for fewer chances than usual. That part of the slump is real.

But the season says more than the slump. At five on five the Penguins get 57% of the expected goals with Dewar on the ice, more than five points better than when he sits. That's a depth player doing the depth job well. Evolving-Hockey liked him last season too (2.2 wins above replacement, 42nd among forwards), though they noted his results ran well ahead of his chances, and he drew more penalties than he took. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows a dump-and-chase player who carries the puck in on just 23% of his entries. Watch the on-ice numbers. If they hold, the points tend to follow.
headline: Dewar's slump hides a solid depth season
